scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance for Management of Stray Cattle
description:
The Scheme of Assistance for Management of Stray Cattle is an initiative by the Government of India aimed at addressing the issue of stray cattle in urban and rural areas.

This scheme was launched in the year 2019 under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to state governments and Union Territories for the management and welfare of stray cattle.

The scheme aims to reduce the population of stray cattle and ensure their proper care and management.

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to facilitate the establishment of cow shelters and gaushalas.

The scheme also aims to promote the adoption of stray cattle by individuals and organizations.

Financial assistance under this scheme is provided to state governments for the construction of shelters for stray cattle.

The financial assistance is up to INR 1 lakh per shelter.

The scheme also provides for the establishment of mobile veterinary units for the treatment of stray cattle.

Each mobile veterinary unit is provided with a financial assistance of INR 5 lakh.

The scheme encourages the involvement of non-governmental organizations and local bodies in the management of stray cattle.

The eligibility criteria for availing assistance under this scheme primarily include the state governments and Union Territories.

There are no specific age limits or educational qualifications required for individuals to participate in the scheme.

However, the implementing authorities must ensure that the funds are utilized for the intended purpose.

The application process for state governments to avail of the scheme involves submitting a detailed project proposal.

The project proposal must include the estimated cost, the number of shelters to be constructed, and the management plan for the stray cattle.

The required documents for the application include a resolution from the state government, project reports, and a detailed financial plan.

The timeline for the submission of project proposals is typically set by the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

Once the proposals are approved, the funds are disbursed to the respective state governments.

The disbursement of funds is generally done in two installments.

The first installment is released upon approval of the project proposal.

The second installment is released after the completion of the project and submission of utilization certificates.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The contact details for the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying can be found on their official website.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of awareness campaigns to educate the public about the welfare of stray cattle.

It encourages community participation in the management and care of stray cattle.

The scheme has provisions for the training of personnel involved in the management of stray cattle.

This training includes veterinary care, feeding, and shelter management.

The scheme has received positive feedback from various states for its potential to improve the welfare of stray cattle.

States like Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh have actively implemented the scheme.

The scheme also aims to reduce the incidents of road accidents caused by stray cattle.

It is estimated that thousands of cattle roam the streets in urban areas, leading to safety concerns.

The scheme also addresses the issue of stray cattle affecting agricultural productivity.

Stray cattle often damage crops and create conflicts between farmers and cattle owners.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the government to promote animal welfare in the country.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 100 crore for the implementation of this scheme.

This budget is aimed at providing financial assistance to various states for effective management of stray cattle.

The scheme is expected to create job opportunities in the animal husbandry sector.

It aims to promote sustainable practices in managing stray cattle.

The scheme also encourages the use of technology in tracking and managing stray cattle populations.

States are encouraged to develop mobile applications for reporting stray cattle.

The scheme has provisions for monitoring and evaluation to assess the impact of the program.

Regular audits are conducted to ensure the proper utilization of funds.

The scheme is aligned with the National Animal Disease Control Programme.

It aims to control the population of stray cattle while ensuring their welfare.

The government has recognized the importance of managing stray cattle for public health and safety.

The scheme also includes provisions for the rehabilitation of stray cattle.

This includes providing veterinary care and nutrition to stray animals.

The scheme is expected to enhance the overall quality of life for stray cattle.

It aims to create a more humane approach to dealing with stray animals.

The government encourages local bodies to take initiative in the management of stray cattle.

This includes forming committees to oversee the implementation of the scheme at the local level.

The scheme is a significant step towards addressing the challenges posed by stray cattle in India.

It reflects the government's commitment to animal welfare and sustainable development.

The scheme is expected to have a long-term impact on the management of stray cattle.

It aims to create a balance between animal welfare and public safety.

The government continues to seek feedback from stakeholders to improve the scheme.

The scheme is part of a larger framework of animal welfare policies in India.

It aims to create a more organized approach to managing stray cattle populations.

The implementation of this scheme is crucial for urban planning and rural development.

The government is committed to ensuring that stray cattle are treated with dignity and respect.

This scheme is an important initiative in the context of India's growing urbanization and population.
